newsitem.title: USA: Tenet to merge with OrNda.
newsitem.headline: Tenet to merge with OrNda.

text.p: Tenet Healthcare Corp has agreed to acquire OrNda HealthCorp for about $1.8 billion in a tax-free stock transaction, the companies said on Thursday.
The boards of Tenet and OrNda approved a definitive agreement on the transaction Wednesday night, they said.
Under the agreement, OrNda shareholders will receive 1.35 Tenet shares for each share of OrNda.
Based on about 60 million fully diluted OrNda shares at Wednesday's closing price of 22-1/8, OrNda shareholders will receive $1.8 billion in Tenet stock, the companies said.

The deal is expected to be accretive to Tenet's earnings and will result in $70 million in annual cost savings, interest reductions and operating synergies following the first full year of combined operations, they said.
The pooling-of-interests transaction will create a consolidated company with pro forma earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of about $1.5 billion.
The combined company will have pro forma revenues of about $8.56 billion and operate 126 acute care hospials in 22 states, principally in the Sun Belt region of the U.S.
As part of the agreement, each of the companies is entitled to receive a termination fee of $50 million from the other if the merger is not completed.
Tenet has granted OrNda an option to buy about 10.5 percent of Tenet's common stock. and OrNda has granted Tenet an option to buy 19.9 percent of OrNda's common under certain circumstances.
The companies hope to close the deal in early March 1997. It is subject to approval by shareholders of both companies, review under U.S. antitrust law, and other regulatory approvals.
The two companies said the transaction values OrNda at $3.1 billion.
Tenet, based in Santa Barbara, Calif., is the second largest investor-owned health care company in the U.S. It owns and operates 76 acute care hopsitals and related businesses in 13 states.

OrNda, based in Nashville, Tenn., is the third largest investor-owned hospital management companiny in the U.S. It provides inpatient and outpatient health care services, principally through its 50 acute care hopsitals in urban and suburban communities in 15 states.
